title: snp: collapse split unreliable recv/send size thresholds
body:
This normalizes SNP unreliable sizing back to a single envelope and removes the recv-side divergence introduced in plaintext chunk ingestion.

The current split between `k_cbMaxUnreliableMsgSizeSend`, `k_cbMaxUnreliableSegmentSizeRecv`, and `k_cbMaxUnreliableMsgSizeRecv` creates an asymmetric policy surface between TX admission and RX reassembly that does not align with the existing SNP buffering model. In particular, `ProcessPlainTextDataChunk` is now performing an additional pre-reassembly bounds gate on `(int64)nOffset + cbSegmentSize` and per-segment size before `SNP_ReceiveUnreliableSegment`, while the unreliable path already keys message assembly off the segment ring / buffered-unreliable bookkeeping.

That extra gate is effectively duplicating invariants outside the reassembly path and couples frame parsing to a derived recv budget (`k_nMaxBufferedUnreliableSegments * k_cbSteamNetworkingSocketsMaxPlaintextPayloadRecv`). For SNP this is the wrong layer to encode a synthetic aggregate cap: plaintext frame decode should remain concerned with extracting the wire representation and dispatching the fragment, not second-guessing the unreliable assembler with a separately maintained recv-side policy constant.

This patch therefore:

- collapses the send-side constant naming back to the canonical `k_cbMaxUnreliableMsgSize`
- removes the recv-only aggregate/segment constants and associated compile-time relationship check
- restores direct dispatch from plaintext chunk decode into `SNP_ReceiveUnreliableSegment`
- keeps the storage declaration aligned with the canonical plaintext payload bound instead of introducing an alias solely for recv-side policy

Net effect is that SNP unreliable handling returns to a single sizing contract, avoiding parser/reassembler policy skew and reducing OOD complexity in the hot path. This also prevents the plaintext decoder from carrying transport-policy assumptions that belong in the unreliable segment accumulator.

## SNP frames

SNP encrypted payload is a sequence of frames.  Each frame begins with an 8-bit
frame type / flags field.

### Unreliable message segment

Encodes a segment of an unreliable message.  (Often, an entire message.)

    00emosss [message_num] [offset] [size] data

    e: 0: There's more data after ths in the unreliable message.

       1: This is the last segment in the unreliable message.
    m: encoded size of message_num

           0: 16-bits
           1: 32-bits
       Subsequent segments: message number field is relative to previous
           0: no message number field follows, assume 1 greater than previous segment
           1: Var-int encoded offset from previous follows
